title: NUS / City now
description: Zone demand, surge, congestion. Scores near 0 at the small seed are expected.

list.name: zone_id
list.label: Zone
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT toString(zone_id) FROM nus.hotspot_history WHERE computed_at >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 300
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT toString(zone_id) FROM nus.hotspot_history WHERE computed_at >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 300

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    zone_id,
    demand_score,
    open_requests,
    available_drivers,
    surge_multiplier,
    period,
    last_computed
FROM (
    SELECT
        zone_id,
        argMax(demand_score, computed_at) AS demand_score,
        argMax(open_requests, computed_at) AS open_requests,
        argMax(available_drivers, computed_at) AS available_drivers,
        argMax(surge_multiplier, computed_at) AS surge_multiplier,
        argMax(period, computed_at) AS period,
        max(computed_at) AS last_computed
    FROM nus.hotspot_history
    WHERE computed_at >= now() - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE
    GROUP BY zone_id
) AS latest
ORDER BY demand_score DESC

panels.title: Demand score, and the surge it sets (selected zone)
panels.description: Both are dimensionless, which is the only reason they share an axis: the score is roughly 0..1 and the multiplier starts at 1.0. The pair is the point - surge is derived from the score, so the two lines moving apart means the derivation is stale, not that demand changed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT computed_at AS time, demand_score, surge_multiplier
FROM nus.hotspot_history
WHERE zone_id = '${zone_id}'
  AND $__timeFilter(computed_at)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Open requests vs free drivers (selected zone)
panels.description: Both are counts of the same kind of thing, so one axis is honest. The gap between them is the imbalance surge exists to close.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT computed_at AS time, open_requests, available_drivers
FROM nus.hotspot_history
WHERE zone_id = '${zone_id}'
  AND $__timeFilter(computed_at)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Congestion factor (selected zone)
panels.description: 1.0 is free-flow and higher is slower. Split from the sample counts below: a factor that lives between 1 and 2 is a flat line at the bottom of a chart scaled to hundreds of samples.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT computed_at AS time, congestion_factor
FROM nus.segment_traffic_history
WHERE zone_id = '${zone_id}'
  AND $__timeFilter(computed_at)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: How much evidence that factor rests on (selected zone)
panels.description: Real position reports behind each reading, and the road segments it was applied to. A congestion factor computed from three samples is a guess with a decimal point.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT computed_at AS time, speed_samples, segments_updated
FROM nus.segment_traffic_history
WHERE zone_id = '${zone_id}'
  AND $__timeFilter(computed_at)
ORDER BY time
